title: Lee Tusman - Lower Dimensional Dungeons
speaker: Lee Tusman
description:
This talk is from the 2020 virtual Roguelike Celebration:
https://roguelike.club/event2020.html

Lee Tusman is a New York-based new media artist and educator interested in the application of the radical ethos of collectives and DIY culture to the creation of, aesthetics, and open-source distribution methods of digital culture. He works in code, collage, sound and text.  His artistic output includes interactive media, video art, net art, experimental videogames, sound art, websites, twitter bots and micro-power radio stations. His work has been shown at museums, galleries, artist-run spaces and virtual environments. He studied at Brandeis University and received his MFA at UCLA in Design Media Arts. He is Assistant Professor of New Media and Computer Science at Purchase College.

In this lightning talk he discusses the concept of lower-dimensional dungeons and:
- How creating a one-dimensional roguelike is a beginner-friendly approach to making your first (or later) roguelike game
- A history of other one-dimensional dungeons including Santiago Zapata's tweet-roguelikes, Line Wobbler (a dungeon crawl but not a roguelike), one-dimensional roguelike Cosmic Crown, branching narrative as a form of 1d, 1dimensional chess variants, and a few other 1dimensional action games
- His own examples of one-dimensional roguelikes and design considerations, coding approaches
- Pointers for directions things can go, demake ideas for turning other 2d roguelikes into 1d

Find him on Twitter: https://twitter.com/2sman2sman
Santiago Zapata's work: https://slashie.net/
Line Wobbler: https://wobblylabs.com/projects/wobbler
